**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0560), Paper 2 - Modern World History Since 1870, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions. TWO questions must be chosen from SECTION A, ONE from SECTION B and ONE other from SECTION C. One of the two questions chosen from SECTION A must be a Starred question (1A\* or 1B\*). Maps should be used to illustrate answers where appropriate. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION A - CAMEROON SINCE 1850.** Question one is compulsory. Answer either 1A\* or 1B\* and one other Question from this section.

**1B\* (Starred question)**

Study this extract on the transition between the Federal Republic of Cameroon and the United Republic of Cameroon and then answer questions (a)-(d) which follow. (The maximum mark for each sub-question is indicated in brackets).

> ...The Federal Republic of Cameroon was a two-state federation born from the plebiscite organised in the Southern Cameroons in ...by an international organisation whose specialised organ was in charge of preparing the territory for self -rule. By the 1970s, the reasons for adopting a two-state federation were considered no longer valid. West Cameroonians in particular felt it was a real financial burden standing on their own as a federated state. **[line 5]**
>
> On the 6th of May 1972, after informing the Political Bureau of the ruling party, Ahidjo addressed the National Assembly and stated ...Although most services have been federalised, the budget of West Cameroon is still experiencing difficulties in spite of balanced subsidy. ...He also addressed the issues of national unity, reunification, the building of single unified party and the construction of a modern and efficient state...The President informed Cameroonians that he would consult them through a referendum on the question.
>
> The President of the Federal Republic scheduled the national consultation on... A day after voting, President Ahidjo addressed the nation and thanked Cameroonians for the peaceful referendum. The referendum had produced a 99.99 vote. Thereafter, a new constitution was adopted for Cameroon with a significant change of name from the Federal Republic to the United Republic of Cameroon. **[line 10]**

*Source: Adapted from: Cameroon: Abrogation of Federalism in Cameroon 1972- A Historical Analysis by Victor Julius Ngoh.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) In which year was the plebiscite mentioned in *line 1* organised in the Southern Cameroons?
(ii) Which international organisation supervised the plebiscite mentioned in a (i) above?
(iii) Name the **two** states that made up the Federal Republic of Cameroon.

(1+1+2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) 1961 [1 mark].** The UN-supervised plebiscite took place on 11 February 1961.

**(ii) The United Nations Organisation (UNO) [1 mark].** Its Trusteeship Council and the General Assembly were in charge of preparing the Southern Cameroons, a trust territory under British administration, for self-rule or independence.

**(iii) East Cameroon and West Cameroon [1 mark each].** East Cameroon was the former French Cameroon (the Republic of Cameroon), and West Cameroon was the former British Southern Cameroons. The federation came into being on 1 October 1961.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Give **two** reasons why by 1972 the reasons for the two state-Federation were considered no longer valid. (*line 3*).
(ii) Apart from the financial burden on the state of West Cameroon (*line 5*) give any **two** reasons not mentioned in the text why some West Cameroonians were no longer enthusiastic about the federation by 1972.
(iii) Give the name of any Prime Minister of West Cameroon whose government (*line 8*) experienced budgetary difficulties.

(2+2+1 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Any two reasons [2 marks].**
(1) The federal guarantees had been emptied of content. Since 1961 power had been concentrated in the hands of the federal President (federal inspectors in the states, federal control of important services), so the two states had little real autonomy.
(2) The single party (the Cameroon National Union, created in 1966) had replaced the party competition of the early 1960s, which made the political reasons for separate states seem outdated.
(3) Keeping two state governments and parliaments next to the federal institutions was costly and duplicated administration, and the leadership said that national unity and integration had advanced enough to do without it.

**(ii) Any two reasons [2 marks].**
(1) West Cameroonians felt that the federal government neglected the economic development of their region and that important activities (ports, trade and services) were drawn to the East.
(2) They felt dominated by the larger French-speaking East in the federal institutions and the civil service, and feared for the future of their English-speaking identity, legal and educational traditions.
(3) The dissolution of the political parties into the single party in 1966 and the loss of political choice reduced the voice of West Cameroon.

**(iii) Any one name [1 mark].** John Ngu Foncha (Prime Minister of West Cameroon from 1961), Augustine Ngom Jua (from 1965) or Salomon Tandeng Muna (from 1968, Prime Minister when the federation was abolished). The extract refers to the early 1970s, so S. T. Muna fits best, but any of the three is acceptable.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Which was the ruling party (*line 6*) whose political bureau was consulted by Ahidjo on the need to abolish the Federation?
(ii) Apart from the reasons in the extract advanced by Ahidjo, which **3** other reasons were given to justify the need to change from a federal to a unitary system of government? (*lines 7-9*).
(iii) Why did Ahidjo have to consult the National Assembly (*line 7*) on the question of abolishing the Federation?

(1+3+1 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The Cameroon National Union (CNU) [1 mark].** It was the single ruling party, formed in 1966 by the merger of the main parties of East and West Cameroon.

**(ii) Any three other reasons [1 mark each].**
(1) To end the duplication of institutions and the conflicts of authority between the federal and the state governments, which slowed down decisions.
(2) To cut the high cost of running three levels of government (federal, East and West) and so save money for development.
(3) To allow a single national development plan and a better use of the country's resources, to speed up economic development.
(4) Because the federal form was presented as a colonial legacy that kept two peoples divided; a unitary state would remove the remaining differences between East and West.
(5) Because West Cameroon could not carry its financial costs without federal subsidies, so the state structure was no longer justified.

**(iii) Reason [1 mark].** The National Assembly was the elected legislative body, representing the people of both states, and the 1961 Constitution gave it a part in any change of the constitutional order. Consulting it gave the decision a legal and political legitimacy; Ahidjo then also went directly to the people through a referendum.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Write down the precise date when the referendum was organised in Cameroon?
(ii) Give the name of the new constitution (*line 13*) which Cameroon adopted after the referendum.
(iii) What important changes occurred in Cameroon following the abolition of the federation.

(1+1+4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) 20 May 1972 [1 mark].** The referendum was held on that date; the extract notes the result as 99.99 per cent.

**(ii) The Constitution of the United Republic of Cameroon [1 mark].** It was adopted after the referendum and promulgated on 2 June 1972.

**(iii) Four changes [1 mark each].**
1. The name of the country became the United Republic of Cameroon, and the federal system was replaced by a unitary state.
2. The two state governments and parliaments (East and West Cameroon) were abolished and replaced by one government and one National Assembly for the whole country.
3. The country was divided into administrative provinces (seven at first) headed by governors appointed by the President, with divisions and districts below them, so the administration was centralised.
4. Power was concentrated in the President (with the single party, the CNU); national symbols changed over time (for example 20 May became the National Day, and the two-star flag was changed to one star in 1975), and West Cameroon lost its separate institutions and special position.
